knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A sign-off describes the machine before a change. After a change it is not current, so the learner stops and has the machine state and authority reconfirmed.
An unexpected restart changes the energy state without the knowledge of those nearby, so it is a stop-and-reauthorise event. A tidy floor or a quiet shift is not a trigger.
Handover is restricted until the owner confirms outstanding restricted work and who decides restart and chemical matters.

practicalCriteria: Identifies the stop-and-reauthorise triggers in a fictional case: unexpected restart, contractor entry and shifted boundary.
Records a simulated machine change after sign-off with time, area, what changed, observation, source, people informed and restriction, and makes no safety claim.
Refers a simulated restart to the mock authorised person, and does not resume work on the earlier sign-off.
Restricts a simulated handover and names the owner of each outstanding decision.
passRule: All four practical criteria observed as met in a desk exercise. The knowledge check result is not a practical pass, and this assessment is not a plant-safety sign-off, isolation authority or restart approval.
evidenceRequired: Restricted handover record with named decision owners
Assessor observation note for each practical criterion
stopWorkCriteria: Work continued after a simulated machine change
Earlier sign-off relied on after the change
Machine started or checked by trial start by the learner
Handover completed with outstanding decisions unassigned
